title: Interview setup; Pioneer grandparents
description: Cathy Naugle begins the interview by confirming biographical details with Phyllis McArthur. McArthur explains that her maternal grandparents were pioneers in Clearwater County who started the first telephone office there.

title: Parents' marriage; Family farm
description: McArthur describes her parents' marriage and their lives farming in the Weippe area. She then lists her five siblings and discusses the differences in family sizes between generations.

title: Marriage and business; Raising daughters
description: She discusses her marriage to Jarrell McArthur in 1936 and their purchase of an appliance business in 1953. She also provides details about their two daughters, Eleanor and the late Janet.

title: Education and retirement; Community organizations
description: McArthur recounts her education, including a brief stint at Kidman Business College, and explains why she chose not to return to school. She then details her extensive volunteer work with the Chamber of Commerce and the hospital auxiliary.

title: Rural versus urban life; Family memories
description: The interview concludes with McArthur's thoughts on the advantages of small-town living versus city life. She also discusses her relationship with her mother and her struggles with a poor memory regarding her childhood.

title: Grandmotherhood; courtship refusal; retirement
description: The conversation begins with Phyllis explaining her close bond with her granddaughters and her role as a supportive grandmother since their mother passed away. She declines to discuss the details of how she met her husband, preferring not to share her romantic history. The discussion moves to her retirement from business and her plans to travel with her husband.

title: Difficult stepmother; Depression memories
description: Phyllis describes her troubled relationship with her father's second wife, whom she characterizes as jealous and difficult. When asked about historical events, she recalls little about the Great Depression or World War II, noting that her family's farm insulated them from hard times.

title: Self-education; churchgoing
description: She discusses her belief in self-education and her willingness to learn new skills, such as parliamentary procedure, despite her age. Phyllis then explains her complex relationship with organized religion—supporting the church financially but choosing not to attend services due to negative childhood experiences with forced religion.

title: Rural advice; media preferences
description: When asked for advice to women moving to rural areas, Phyllis suggests they must be self-reliant and resilient. She lists her and her husband's magazine subscriptions and television preferences, emphasizing her dislike for comedies and preference for serious dramas and love stories.

title: Gender identity; robbery; mental strength
description: Phyllis asserts her domestic competence while identifying with traditionally masculine traits and preferring male companionship. The interview concludes with her recounting the traumatic event of her husband shooting a robber in their store, and her reflections on maintaining mental strength through life's hardships.
